newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: McDonalds to invest $7 million in Yugoslavia - paper.
newsitem.headline: McDonalds to invest $7 million in Yugoslavia - paper.

text.p: The U.S. fast food chain McDonald's Corp plans to invest around $7 million in its Yugoslav operations, the Belgrade daily Politika reported on Monday.
"We plan to 'grow' to 60 restaurants in Yugoslavia by the next century," McDonalds Central Europe operations vice president Branimir Lalic was quoted by the paper as saying.
At present, McDonalds operates eight restaurants in Yugoslavia and plans to raise their numbers to 13 in 1997, 21 in 1998 and 37 by 1999, Lalic said.
"Next spring we are opening a restaurant in Nis, then in Subotica, and later in Kragujevac and three more in Belgrade," Lalic said.
Most of the restaurants would be franchised to private entrepreneurs, he said.
McDonalds' final objective is 100 restaurants in Serbia and Montenegro, which comprise rump Yugoslavia.
No-one at Genex-McDonalds, the Yugoslav joint venture company, was immediately available for comment.
Of the total investments, around $1 million will be spent on the restaurant in the northern town of Subotica.
Another $2 million will be invested in a chicken and meat processing plant, Frilo, to be set up by Belgrade's Frikom and the international firm L&O.
The plant, to be opened by the end of the year, is expected to grow into a regional supplier for McDonalds, Lalic said.
Pie production for Yugoslavia and eastern European countries, organized by the British firm Kitchen Range will cost $1 million.
Fresh Bakeries of the U.S. and Yugoslavia's Zitorprodukt will jointly produce bread rolls for Yugoslavia, Macedonia and Albania. The deal is worth around $700,000.

Yugoslavia's Genex-McDonalds has been chosen to assist and develop the restaurant chains in Macedonia and Albania, to supply neighbouring countries and to become the backbone of future regional integration with McDonald's firms in Romania, Bulgaria, Hungary and Slovenia, Lalic said.
